symbols.name: T
symbols.def: Number of adaptively randomized decision occasions.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: Decision-occasion index.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Number of treatment arms.

symbols.name: \mathcal A
symbols.def: Set of randomized treatment arms.

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: Dimension of the stacked causal parameter.

symbols.name: \Theta
symbols.def: Parameter space for the stacked arm-specific marginal moment target.

symbols.name: \mathcal X
symbols.def: Context space observed before randomization.

symbols.name: X_t
symbols.def: Context observed at occasion \(t\).

symbols.name: Y_t(a)
symbols.def: Potential outcome at occasion \(t\) under arm \(a\in\mathcal A\).

symbols.name: W_t
symbols.def: Full-data vector \(W_t=(X_t,(Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A})\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Law of the sequential full-data draws and adaptive randomization.

symbols.name: A_t
symbols.def: Treatment randomized at occasion \(t\).

symbols.name: Y_t
symbols.def: Observed outcome \(Y_t=Y_t(A_t)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F_t
symbols.def: Filtration generated by observations and randomizations through occasion \(t\).

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: Dimension of the adaptive policy state.

symbols.name: \mathsf H
symbols.def: State space for the adaptive recursion.

symbols.name: \eta_t
symbols.def: Policy state after occasion \(t\), measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_t\).

symbols.name: \eta_0
symbols.def: Policy state before the first adaptive randomization.

symbols.name: \Pi
symbols.def: Policy map whose arm probabilities sum to one for every context and state.

symbols.name: \pi_t
symbols.def: Logged randomization probability \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})=\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta_{t-1})\).

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: Uniform exploration floor.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Common envelope for the causal score over the triangular-array class.

symbols.name: D_1
symbols.def: Common envelope for the first parameter derivative of the causal score.

symbols.name: D_2
symbols.def: Common envelope for the second parameter derivative of the causal score.

symbols.name: h_-
symbols.def: Common lower singular-value bound for the population Jacobian.

symbols.name: L_\Pi
symbols.def: Common Lipschitz modulus for the policy map.

symbols.name: \omega_-
symbols.def: Common lower eigenvalue bound for every basin score covariance.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: Common separation modulus for the population causal moment away from its root.

symbols.name: s_\Theta
symbols.def: Common interior-radius bound for the causal moment root.

symbols.name: g
symbols.def: Stacked arm-specific causal estimating function evaluated at an action, context, potential outcome, and parameter.

symbols.name: M_P
symbols.def: Population causal moment \(M_P(\theta)=E_P[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)]\).

symbols.name: \theta^*
symbols.def: Distinguished marginal causal moment root satisfying \(M_P(\theta^*)=0\).

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.def: Common radius for local exact-root search, fixed so that the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\) lies inside the smoothness and interiority neighborhood and \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Prespecified contrast of the causal moment parameter.

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: Causal contrast \(\tau=c^\top\theta^*\).

symbols.name: \xi_t
symbols.def: Adaptive IPW score \(\xi_t=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}g(a,X_t,Y_t;\theta^*)/\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\).

symbols.name: S_T
symbols.def: Cumulative score \(S_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t\).

symbols.name: \langle S\rangle_T
symbols.def: Predictable quadratic variation \(\langle S\rangle_T=\sum_{t=1}^TE_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\).

symbols.name: [S]_T
symbols.def: Realized quadratic variation \([S]_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t\xi_t^\top\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: Population Jacobian \(H=\partial_\theta E_P[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)]|_{\theta=\theta^*}\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Number of candidate deterministic tail attractors.

symbols.name: \bar\eta_j
symbols.def: Candidate attractor state indexed by \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: Tail basin selected by the adaptive recursion.

symbols.name: \mathcal J
symbols.def: Positive-mass support of the selected basin, \(\mathcal J=\{j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:P(J=j)>0\}\).

symbols.name: \bar\eta_J
symbols.def: Selected attractor \(\bar\eta_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\bar\eta_j\).

symbols.name: p_j
symbols.def: Basin probability \(p_j=P(J=j)\).

symbols.name: \Omega_j
symbols.def: Basin score covariance obtained by replacing \(\pi_t\) with \(\Pi(\cdot\mid X_t,\bar\eta_j)\) in \(E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\).

symbols.name: \Omega_J
symbols.def: Selected-basin score covariance \(\Omega_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\Omega_j\).

symbols.name: V_j
symbols.def: Basin estimator covariance \(V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}\).

symbols.name: V_J
symbols.def: Selected-basin covariance \(V_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Gaussian innovation independent of \(\sigma(J)\).

symbols.name: G_T
symbols.def: Empirical IPW moment \(G_T(\theta)=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}g(a,X_t,Y_t;\theta)/\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\).

symbols.name: \widetilde\theta_T
symbols.def: Measurable preliminary approximate minimizer of the empirical IPW moment norm.

symbols.name: \mathcal Z_T
symbols.def: Local empirical-root set \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\).

symbols.name: E_T
symbols.def: Exact-root existence event \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\theta_T
symbols.def: Total measurable IPW-Z estimator obtained by selecting an exact empirical root from \(\mathcal Z_T\) on \(E_T\) and using \(\widetilde\theta_T\) on \(E_T^c\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_T
symbols.def: Contrast estimator \(\widehat\tau_T=c^\top\widehat\theta_T\).

symbols.name: \widehat H_T
symbols.def: Empirical derivative \(\widehat H_T=\partial_\theta G_T(\widehat\theta_T)\).

symbols.name: \widehat\xi_t
symbols.def: IPW score \(\xi_t\) evaluated at \(\widehat\theta_T\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Omega_T
symbols.def: Feasible realized score covariance \(\widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top\).

symbols.name: \mathcal E_T
symbols.def: Uniform invertibility event \(\mathcal E_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2,\ \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_T)\ge\omega_-/2\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat V_T
symbols.def: Event-truncated realized-QV sandwich \(\widehat V_T=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_T}\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}+\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_T^c}I_d\); the inverse is evaluated only on \(\mathcal E_T\).

symbols.name: T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)
symbols.def: Realized-QV studentized statistic for contrast \(c\).

symbols.name: \Sigma
symbols.def: Fixed sandwich matrix used by a conventional Wald report.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: Nominal noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: \Phi
symbols.def: Standard normal distribution function.

symbols.name: z_{1-\alpha/2}
symbols.def: Quantile \(z_{1-\alpha/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).

symbols.name: C_T^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)
symbols.def: Two-sided Wald interval based on the deterministic sandwich \(\Sigma\).

symbols.name: r_T
symbols.def: Cesaro policy-state error tolerance at horizon \(T\).

symbols.name: \delta_T
symbols.def: Tail probability in the uniform attraction modulus at horizon \(T\).

symbols.name: e_T
symbols.def: Common triangular-array error envelope \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak P_T
symbols.def: Finite-attractor adaptive-experiment law class at horizon \(T\), indexed by fixed common constants and moduli.

symbols.name: R_{t,a}
symbols.def: Independent centered two-point innovation with \(P(R_{t,a}=+1)=P(R_{t,a}=-1)=1/2\), independent across occasions and arms and independent of the contexts.

symbols.name: \sigma_a
symbols.def: Arbitrary fixed reward-innovation scale for arm \(a\) in the bounded Rademacher analogue.

symbols.name: \Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}
symbols.def: Guo--Xu no-intercept arm-specific ridge Gram state after occasion \(t\).

symbols.name: b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}
symbols.def: Guo--Xu no-intercept arm-specific ridge response state after occasion \(t\).

symbols.name: \widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}
symbols.def: Arm-specific no-intercept ridge slope \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\).

symbols.name: q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}
symbols.def: Inverse ridge Gram state \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=1/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\).

symbols.name: Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t
symbols.def: Sufficient state \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2},q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) for the bounded clipped-LinUCB recursion.

symbols.name: \mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Compact set \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{GX}}=[-M_{\mathrm{GX}},M_{\mathrm{GX}}]^2\times[0,1]^2\) containing every augmented-chain state from the prescribed initialization.

symbols.name: \mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Compact index set \(\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}=[-1,1]^2\) for the two initial slopes; it is not the state space of the augmented Markov chain.

symbols.name: \iota_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Embedding \(\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\) of an initial-slope pair into the augmented chain.

symbols.name: m_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Number of distinct deterministic projected slope limits quantified in the bounded Guo--Xu dynamics question.

symbols.name: \bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_j
symbols.def: Distinct deterministic projected slope limit indexed by \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m_{\mathrm{GX}}\}\) in the bounded Guo--Xu dynamics question.

symbols.name: P_{\eta_0}
symbols.def: Probability law of the augmented bounded-noise Guo--Xu chain started from \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)\) for \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\).

symbols.name: J_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Tail-measurable index of the attained deterministic limit of the slope projection of the augmented bounded Guo--Xu chain.

symbols.name: B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j
symbols.type: subset of the compact initial-slope index set
symbols.def: Positive-probability basin \(B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j=\{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}:P_{\eta_0}(J_{\mathrm{GX}}=j)>0\}\).

symbols.name: K_0
symbols.def: Compact collection of initial slopes contained in the union of basin interiors relative to \(\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\).

symbols.name: r_T(K_0)
symbols.def: Compact-set Cesaro attraction tolerance at horizon \(T\) in the bounded-dynamics question.

symbols.name: \delta_T(K_0)
symbols.def: Compact-set attraction failure probability at horizon \(T\) in the bounded-dynamics question.

symbols.name: \Theta_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Parameter space that a future Guo--Xu inference result would have to specify separately from the dynamics question.

symbols.name: g_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Causal score that a future Guo--Xu inference result would have to specify separately from the dynamics question.

symbols.name: \theta^*_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Unique causal-score root that a future Guo--Xu inference result would have to define and verify.

symbols.name: c_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Nonzero contrast that a future Guo--Xu inference result would have to specify.

symbols.name: \tau_{\mathrm{GX}}
symbols.def: Scalar target \(\tau_{\mathrm{GX}}=c_{\mathrm{GX}}^\top\theta^*_{\mathrm{GX}}\) that a future Guo--Xu inference result would have to define.

symbols.name: P^{\dagger}
symbols.def: Law of the explicit bounded two-basin adaptive experiment in the directional--matrix separation construction.

assumptions.condition: The vectors \(W_1,\ldots,W_T\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).
Conditional on \(X_t\) and \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), the action \(A_t\) is drawn from the logged distribution \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\) independently of \((Y_t(a))_{a\in\mathcal A}\).
For every \(t\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), context, and realized history, \(\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\ge\varepsilon\).
The common envelope satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,\theta\in\Theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2\le B\) almost surely.
constants: \(B<\infty\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: The map \(\theta\mapsto g(a,x,y;\theta)\) is continuously differentiable on a common open neighborhood of \(\operatorname{conv}(\Theta)\), with \(\|\partial_\theta g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_1\) there, and is twice continuously differentiable on the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), with \(\|\partial_\theta^2 g(a,x,y;\theta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le D_2\) throughout that ball.
constants: \(D_1,D_2<\infty\) and \(\rho>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law
\(\kappa(u)>0\) for every \(u>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

standard.name: Uniform separation of a Z-functional root

constants: \(s_\Theta>0\), fixed across every horizon and member law
\(h_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: The common policy modulus satisfies \(\sup_{a\in\mathcal A,x\in\mathcal X}|\Pi(a\mid x,\eta)-\Pi(a\mid x,\eta')|\le L_\Pi\|\eta-\eta'\|_2\) for all \(\eta,\eta'\in\mathsf H\).
constants: \(L_\Pi<\infty\), fixed across every horizon and member law

assumptions.condition: There is a tail variable \(J\in\mathcal J\), measurable with respect to the sigma-field generated by \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge1}\), such that \(\eta_t\to\bar\eta_J\) almost surely under \(P\).

novel.justification: Finite tail selection describes stochastic-approximation rules with several isolated locally stable equilibria, including clipped policy recursions whose early assignments select a persistent operating regime.

A Cesaro attraction modulus records the fraction of decisions made away from the selected long-run policy. It can be bounded using lock-in tails for stochastic approximation and estimated from replicated adaptive deployments.

assumptions.condition: The common deterministic error envelope satisfies \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\to0\).

novel.justification: The combined envelope is a proposal-specific class-level restriction coupling sampling fluctuation, Cesaro attraction error, and attraction-tail probability. It is directly satisfied by immediately locking finite-state adaptive rules and can be audited from replicated policy paths; Mourrat supplies only the martingale central-limit ingredient used after this envelope is imposed.

assumptions.condition: The basin covariances satisfy \(\Omega_j\succeq\omega_-I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\).
constants: \(\omega_->0\), fixed across every horizon and member law

novel.justification: A common lower eigenvalue bound over every positive-mass basin and every member law is a proposal-specific uniform class restriction, stronger than Saco's pointwise variance-growth condition. It is satisfied by bounded finite-policy families whose arm probabilities stay uniformly positive and whose arm-score covariance spans every target direction; the upper bound \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) follows from the bounded score and overlap conditions and is not primitive.

definitions.name: finite-attractor adaptive-experiment class
definitions.construction: For fixed \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,L_\Pi,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\) and common sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), define \(\mathfrak P_T=\{P:\text{at horizon }T,\ P\text{ satisfies every condition in }\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\ldots,\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}nondegeneracy}\text{ with these same fixed envelopes and moduli}\}\).

definitions.name: adaptive IPW-Z estimator
definitions.construction: First choose a measurable preliminary estimator \(\widetilde\theta_T\in\Theta\) satisfying \(\|G_T(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\le\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)\|_2+T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\), using a fixed measurable tie-breaking rule. Define the compact correspondence \(\mathcal Z_T=\{\theta\in\Theta:G_T(\theta)=0,\ \|\theta-\widetilde\theta_T\|_2\le\rho/2\}\) and \(E_T=\{\mathcal Z_T\ne\varnothing\}\). Continuity of \(G_T\) on compact \(\Theta\) makes \(\mathcal Z_T\) compact, and its standard joint measurability permits a fixed measurable lexicographic compact-set selector. On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\theta_T\) be that selected member of \(\mathcal Z_T\); on \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\).

definitions.name: bounded two-basin separation witness
definitions.construction: For every \(T\ge2\), let \(P^{\dagger}\) be the law with \(K=3\), \(d=2\), \(\Theta=[-1,1]^2\), \(\theta^*=0\), a singleton \(\mathcal X\), and constant \(X_t\). Independently across \(t\) and between arms, let \(Y_t(1)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{2/5},\sqrt{2/5}\}\), let \(Y_t(2)\) be equiprobable on \(\{-\sqrt{1/2},\sqrt{1/2}\}\), and set \(Y_t(3)=0\). Set \(g(1,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta_1,0)^\top\), \(g(2,x,y;\theta)=(0,y-\theta_2)^\top\), and \(g(3,x,y;\theta)=0\). Take \(m=2\), \(q=1\), \(\mathsf H=[0,1]\), \(\bar\eta_1=0\), \(\bar\eta_2=1\), and linearly interpolate the context-free policy between \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,0)=(2/5,1/4,7/20)\) and \(\Pi(\cdot\mid x,1)=(2/5,1/6,13/30)\). Start at \(\eta_0=1/2\), set \(J=1\) if and only if \(A_1=1\), set \(J=2\) otherwise, and put \(\eta_t=\bar\eta_J=J-1\) for every \(t\ge1\).

definitions.name: basin-indexed covariance
definitions.construction: For each \(j\in\mathcal J\), set \(V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}\), \(\Omega_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\Omega_j\), and \(V_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\).

definitions.name: event-truncated realized-QV sandwich
definitions.construction: Set \(\widehat\Omega_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top\) and \(\mathcal E_T=\{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2,\ \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_T)\ge\omega_-/2\}\). Define \(\widehat V_T=\widehat H_T^{-1}\widehat\Omega_T\widehat H_T^{-\top}\) on \(\mathcal E_T\) and \(\widehat V_T=I_d\) on \(\mathcal E_T^c\).

definitions.name: bounded-noise Guo--Xu no-intercept recursion
definitions.construction: Fix \(K=2\), draw \(X_t\) independently and uniformly from \(\{-4,1\}\), and set \(Y_t(1)=1/2+\sigma_1R_{t,1}\) and \(Y_t(2)=1/12+\sigma_2R_{t,2}\), where the \(R_{t,a}\) are independent centered Rademacher innovations and \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) are arbitrary fixed constants declared as part of this bounded analogue; no numerical innovation variances are attributed to Guo and Xu. Keep their no-intercept working model, ridge constant \(\lambda=1\), unit-precision ridge initialization, and updates \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_t^2\), \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}+\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}X_tY_t\), and \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}/\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\). For \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), initialize \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_0=\iota_{\mathrm{GX}}(\eta_0)=(\eta_{0,1},\eta_{0,2},1,1)^\top\), equivalently \(\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=1\) and \(b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{0,a}=\eta_{0,a}\); the published initialization is the included case \(\eta_0=(0,0)^\top\). At occasion \(t\), break every exact index tie in favor of arm \(1\), maximize \(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}X_t+|X_t|\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t-1,a}}\), and then assign the maximizing arm with probability \(0.99\) and the other arm with probability \(0.01\). The process of interest is the slope projection \((\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top\) of \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), not a slope-only Markov chain.

definitions.name: bounded-recursion dynamics certification handle
definitions.construction: Write \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\beta_1,\beta_2,q_1,q_2)^\top\) for a current augmented state. Its induced armwise update is \(q_a^+=q_a/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\) and \(\beta_a^+=(\beta_a+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aXY(a))/(1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2)\). The next clipped-UCB action uses \(\beta_aX+|X|\sqrt{q_a}\), so \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), rather than its two-dimensional slope projection, is the time-homogeneous Markov state. For stochastic-approximation analysis, put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and, for \(t\ge1\), \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Analyze the exact \(1/(t+1)\) recursion for \(\Psi_t\) on an eventually compact region with both normalized Gram coordinates bounded away from zero. At the equal-slope surface, retain every limiting conditional-mean mode generated by the square-root UCB bonus: although the bonus is \(O(t^{-1/2})\), it can make the same arm greedy at both contexts inside an \(O(t^{-1/2})\) switching layer. Thus a closed convexified limiting graph must include these same-arm modes as well as the two opposite-context modes. Any differential-inclusion reduction must verify the closed-graph, compact-convex-value, boundedness, vanishing-perturbation, and martingale-tail conditions for this normalized recursion. Compact-uniform sequences \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\to0\) require a separate quantitative hitting or escape estimate and may not be inferred from pointwise convergence by a finite-cover argument.

statements.statement:
For each \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), write \(\mathcal J_P=\{j:P(J=j)>0\}\), \(p_{P,j}=P(J=j)\), and let \(V_{P,j}\) denote the value of \(V_j\) under \(P\). The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\) and \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_P\). There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\left[\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The strongest label-free distributional conclusion implied by these primitives is the \(P\)-specific finite-mixture approximation
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}
 -\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_P}p_{P,j}\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_{P,j}c}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), there is a subsequence \(T_\ell\to\infty\), a fixed set \(\mathcal J_0\), and limits \(p_j^\infty\) and positive-definite \(V_j^\infty\) such that \(\mathcal J_{P_{T_\ell}}=\mathcal J_0\), \(p_{P_{T_\ell},j}\to p_j^\infty\), and \(V_{P_{T_\ell},j}\to V_j^\infty\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\). Along this subsequence, every fixed contrast has the centered Gaussian-mixture limit with weights \(p_j^\infty\) and projected variances \(c^\top V_j^\infty c\), omitting zero limiting weights. If two positive limiting weights have unequal projected variances, this limit is not Gaussian. In general, the class primitives do not imply stable convergence relative to \(\sigma(J)\), even when all basin covariance matrices are equal.
statements.justification: This theorem derives uniform predictable-QV control, exact-root localization, and a P-specific finite Gaussian-mixture approximation while proving that the basin label itself need not be asymptotically independent of the score.
statements.gap: Guo and Xu prove ordinary Gaussian inference after inverse propensities stabilize and illustrate two policy modes numerically; they do not derive the present uniform label-free finite-mixture approximation, and the frozen primitives cannot support a basin-label-stable limit.
statements.consumer: A HeartSteps-style online learner can use the P-specific repeated-deployment mixture for a prespecified causal excursion contrast without treating an arbitrary tail label as observed asymptotic information.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(g_{t,a}(\theta)=g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\). By the i.i.d.-full-data and sequential-randomization assumptions, and using the overlap bound to justify division,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]
&=E_P\left[E_P\left\{\left.\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}g_{t,a}(\theta^*)}
 {\pi_t(a\mid X_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})}\right|W_t,\mathcal F_{t-1}\right\}\middle|\mathcal F_{t-1}\right]\\
&=E_P\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\right]
=M_P(\theta^*)=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \((\xi_t,\mathcal F_t)\) is a martingale-difference array. Define for this proof
\[
 \Gamma_P(\eta)=E_P\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{g_{t,a}(\theta^*)g_{t,a}(\theta^*)^\top}
 {\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right].
\]
The same conditioning calculation gives
\[
 E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1}),
 \qquad \Omega_j=\Gamma_P(\bar\eta_j).
\]
The bounded-score and overlap assumptions imply \(\|\xi_t\|_2\le B/\varepsilon\). For every unit vector \(u\),
\[
 u^\top\Omega_ju
 \le E_P\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{\|g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\|_2^2}{\Pi(a\mid X_t,\bar\eta_j)}\right]
 \le \frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon},
\]
which proves \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\). The derivative envelope permits differentiation under the finite sum and expectation, and hence
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le E_P\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\|\partial_\theta g_{t,a}(\theta^*)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le KD_1.
\]

For \(p,q\ge\varepsilon\), \(|p^{-1}-q^{-1}|\le|p-q|/\varepsilon^2\). The policy-Lipschitz assumption therefore yields
\[
 \|\Gamma_P(\eta)-\Gamma_P(\eta')\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma\|\eta-\eta'\|_2,
 \qquad L_\Gamma=\frac{KB^2L_\Pi}{\varepsilon^2},
\]
and \(\|\Gamma_P(\eta)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le M_\Gamma:=KB^2/\varepsilon\). On
\[
 \mathcal A_T=\left\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T
 \|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2\le r_T\right\},
\]
we have
\[
 \left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T^c\) the norm is at most \(2M_\Gamma\), and the uniform-attraction-modulus assumption gives \(P(\mathcal A_T^c)\le\delta_T\). Thus
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T+2M_\Gamma\delta_T
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]

We next prove localization rather than assume it. For fixed \(\theta\), sequential randomization and i.i.d. arrivals show that the summands of \(G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\) are mean-zero martingale differences. Their norms are uniformly bounded, so martingale orthogonality gives
\[
 E_P\|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2^2\le C_0/T.
\]
The empirical and population maps are uniformly Lipschitz in \(\theta\), with respective moduli \(D_1/\varepsilon\) and \(KD_1\). For fixed \(x>0\), take a finite mesh of the compact set \(\Theta\) fine enough that these two Lipschitz errors sum to at most \(x/2\). Chebyshev's inequality and the union bound over that fixed mesh then give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\left\{\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 \|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2>x\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Since \(M_P(\theta^*)=0\) and the preliminary estimator obeys its defining approximate-minimum inequality,
\[
 \|M_P(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2
 \le2\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\|G_T(\theta)-M_P(\theta)\|_2
 +T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)=o_P(1)
\]
uniformly. The uniform-root-separation assumption now implies, for every \(u>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\{\|\widetilde\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2\ge u\}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P\{\|M_P(\widetilde\theta_T)\|_2\ge\kappa(u)\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]

At \(\theta^*\), \(G_T(\theta^*)=S_T/T\), so martingale orthogonality and bounded increments give \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. The same entrywise calculation for the derivative score, using the derivative envelope, gives
\[
 R_T:=\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. On the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), the curvature and overlap bounds imply
\[
 \sup_{\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2\le\rho}
 \|\partial_\theta G_T(\theta)-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\|R_T\|_{\mathrm{op}}+D_2\rho/\varepsilon.
\]
The choice of \(\rho\) and the Jacobian lower bound make the right side smaller than \(h_-/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one. On this event, define \(\Psi_T(\theta)=\theta-H^{-1}G_T(\theta)\). Since \(\|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h_-^{-1}\), \(\Psi_T\) is a contraction with constant at most \(1/2\) on the closed \(\rho\)-ball. Moreover,
\[
 \|\Psi_T(\theta)-\theta^*\|_2
 \le\tfrac12\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2+h_-^{-1}\|G_T(\theta^*)\|_2.
\]
The last term is at most \(\rho/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one. The root-interior condition ensures that this closed ball lies in \(\Theta\). Hence the contraction has exactly one fixed point \(\theta_T^0\) in the ball, and
\[
 \|\theta_T^0-\theta^*\|_2
 \le2h_-^{-1}\|G_T(\theta^*)\|_2=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\]
Uniform consistency of \(\widetilde\theta_T\) and the last rate imply that both \(\widetilde\theta_T\) and \(\theta_T^0\) are within \(\rho/4\) of \(\theta^*\) with probability tending uniformly to one. Then \(\theta_T^0\in\mathcal Z_T\), while every member of \(\mathcal Z_T\) lies in the closed \(\rho\)-ball and therefore equals \(\theta_T^0\). Thus \(P(E_T^c)\to0\) uniformly and the selected estimator equals \(\theta_T^0\) except on a uniformly negligible event.

Put \(\Delta_T=\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\). On the preceding event, Taylor's formula and the curvature bound give
\[
 0=G_T(\widehat\theta_T)
 =T^{-1}S_T+H\Delta_T+R_T\Delta_T+R_T^{(2)},
 \qquad
 \|R_T^{(2)}\|_2\le\frac{D_2}{2\varepsilon}\|\Delta_T\|_2^2.
\]
Because \(\Delta_T=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) and \(R_T=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), multiplication by \(\sqrt T H^{-1}\) proves
\[
 \sqrt T\Delta_T+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(T^{-1/2})=O_P(e_T).
\]
The complement of the exact-root event has uniformly vanishing probability, so restoring the fallback does not change this uniform order statement.

It remains to obtain the distributional conclusion without conditioning on the label. Set
\[
 \beta_T=\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\},\qquad
 k_T=\lceil T\beta_T\rceil,\qquad
 \Lambda_T=k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1}).
\]
The vanishing-modulus assumption implies \(k_T/T\to0\), and \(Tr_T/k_T\le\sqrt{r_T}\). Since \(\Lambda_T\) is \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable, the attraction-event calculation gives
\[
 E_P\|\Lambda_T-\Omega_J\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma\frac{Tr_T}{k_T}+2M_\Gamma\delta_T=o(1)
\]
uniformly. With
\[
 B_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T\Gamma_P(\eta_{t-1}),
\]
the same calculation, now accounting for the omitted prefix, yields
\[
 E_P\|B_T-\Omega_J\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le L_\Gamma r_T+M_\Gamma k_T/T+2M_\Gamma\delta_T=o(1).
\]
Consequently \(E_P\|B_T-\Lambda_T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o(1)\) uniformly.

Fix a unit vector \(c\) and put \(a=H^{-\top}c\). The proved upper bound on \(H\) and the assumed lower singular-value bound give
\[
 (KD_1)^{-1}\le\|a\|_2\le h_-^{-1}.
\]
Thus \(|a^\top\xi_t|\le B/(\varepsilon h_-)\), while basin nondegeneracy gives
\[
 a^\top\Omega_Ja\ge v_0:=\frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}>0.
\]
Also \(a^\top\Lambda_Ta\le v_+:=M_\Gamma/h_-^2\). Define the \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable clipped variance
\[
 \lambda_{T,P,c}=\max\{v_0/2,a^\top\Lambda_Ta\}.
\]
Because \(a^\top\Omega_Ja\ge v_0\),
\[
 E_P|a^\top B_Ta-\lambda_{T,P,c}|
 \le \|a\|_2^2E_P\|B_T-\Lambda_T\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\|a\|_2^2E_P\|\Lambda_T-\Omega_J\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o(1)
\]
uniformly in \(P\) and unit \(c\). Apply \(\mathrm{lem:early\text{-}measurable\text{-}martingale\text{-}mixture}\) to \(X_{T,t}=-a^\top\xi_t\), \(\mathcal G_{T,t}=\mathcal F_t\), and \(\lambda_{T,P,c}\). It follows that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_z
 \left|P\left\{-a^\top T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=k_T+1}^T\xi_t\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{\lambda_{T,P,c}}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
The normal CDF is uniformly Lipschitz in its variance on intervals bounded away from zero. Since \(\lambda_{T,P,c}-a^\top\Omega_Ja\to0\) in \(L^1\) uniformly, the expectation in the last display may be replaced by
\[
 E_P\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{a^\top\Omega_Ja}}\right)
 =\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_P}p_{P,j}\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{c^\top V_{P,j}c}}\right).
\]
Martingale orthogonality gives
\[
 E_P\left|a^\top T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\xi_t\right|^2
 \le Ck_T/T=o(1),
\]
so the prefix is negligible uniformly. Finally, the exact-root linearization has a uniformly \(o_P(1)\) remainder because \(e_T\to0\). The limiting mixture densities are uniformly bounded by the common positive variance lower bound, so the usual \(\eta\)-smoothing inequality transfers the preceding approximation through both negligible remainders and proves the asserted uniform CDF formula.

The matrices \(V_{P,j}\) satisfy the common bounds
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_{P,j}
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d.
\]
Indeed, the upper bound uses \(\|H^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le h_-^{-1}\), while the lower bound uses \(\Omega_j\succeq\omega_-I_d\) and \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\). There are finitely many possible supports. Hence every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\) has a subsequence with a constant support and with all finitely many weights and covariance entries convergent. The uniform CDF approximation then gives the claimed subsequential mixture law.

If \(q_j=c^\top V_j^\infty c\) and \(\bar q=\sum_jp_j^\infty q_j\), the second and fourth moments of the limiting mixture are \(\bar q\) and \(3\sum_jp_j^\infty q_j^2\). A centered Gaussian with variance \(\bar q\) has fourth moment \(3\bar q^2\), and the difference is
\[
 3\sum_jp_j^\infty(q_j-\bar q)^2.
\]
It is strictly positive when two positive limiting weights have different projected variances, proving non-Gaussianity.

Finally, stable convergence relative to the label is not implied. For odd \(T\), take \(d=1\), two actions with constant probabilities \((1/2,1/2)\), i.i.d. Rademacher variables \(R_t\), \(Y_t(1)=Y_t(2)=R_t\), and \(g(a,x,y;\theta)=(y-\theta)/2\) on \(\Theta=[-1,1]\). Let the compact state space be the singleton \(\{0\}\), let both candidate attractors and every state equal zero, but set \(J=1\) if \(\sum_{t=1}^TR_t>0\) and \(J=2\) otherwise. The score is bounded and linear, \(M_P(\theta)=-\theta\), \(H=-1\), the root is interior and uniformly separated, the constant policy is Lipschitz and satisfies overlap, and both basin covariances equal one. Thus this triangular sequence satisfies every defining primitive with \(r_T=\delta_T=0\); both labels have probability \(1/2\), and the exact empirical root is \(T^{-1}\sum_tR_t\). With \(h(1)=1\), \(h(2)=-1\), and \(f(x)=\tanh(x)\), the actual joint expectation is
\[
 E\left|\tanh\left(T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^TR_t\right)\right|.
\]
This expectation is bounded away from zero without invoking a limit theorem. Indeed, for \(X_T=T^{-1}(\sum_tR_t)^2\), independence gives \(E[X_T]=1\) and \(E[X_T^2]=3-2/T\le3\). If \(A_T=\{X_T>1/2\}\), then Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 1=E[X_T]\le\tfrac12+E[X_T\mathbf 1_{A_T}]
 \le\tfrac12+\sqrt{3P(A_T)},
\]
so \(P(A_T)\ge1/12\). The displayed joint expectation is therefore at least \(\tanh(1/\sqrt2)/12>0\). By symmetry and oddness, an innovation independent of \(J\) would instead give \(E[h(J)]E[\tanh(-Z)]=0\). Thus the stable-label claim fails inside the frozen class, whereas the marginal mixture approximation remains valid.

statements.statement: Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), \(T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), \(\widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\widehat H_T-H=O_P(e_T)\). Consequently \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\to0\), so the event truncation is asymptotically inactive uniformly, \(\widehat V_T-V_J=O_P(e_T)\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)|\to0\). This uniform statement strictly strengthens Saco's pointwise realized-QV pivot on the conditional finite-attractor class by deriving the variance-ratio, invertibility-event, and inverse-QV controls from the common attraction and exact-root localization controls.
statements.justification: The always-defined truncated sandwich follows the realized basin, is uniformly untruncated asymptotically, and removes the Gaussian scale mixture without estimating basin probabilities.
statements.gap: Saco proves a pointwise self-normalized martingale theorem under abstract variance growth; the unresolved step is uniform verification for an endogenous finite-attractor recursion under common attraction and exact-root localization controls.
statements.consumer: The result gives a feasible standard-normal Wald procedure for causal excursion contrasts in adaptive mobile-health experiments with path-dependent assignment regimes.
statements.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 D_t=\xi_t\xi_t^\top-E_P[\xi_t\xi_t^\top\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}].
\]
Each matrix entry of \(D_t\) is a martingale difference. Since the bounded-score and overlap assumptions give \(\|\xi_t\|_2\le B/\varepsilon\), martingale orthogonality and fixed \(d\) imply
\[
 E_P\left\|T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^TD_t\right\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le C/T.
\]
The operator norm is bounded by the Frobenius norm, so
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly.

On the high-probability exact-root event proved in \(\mathrm{thm:basin\text{-}stable\text{-}ipwz}\), \(\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2=O_P(T^{-1/2})\). The derivative and overlap bounds give
\[
 \|\widehat\xi_t-\xi_t\|_2
 \le\frac{D_1}{\varepsilon}\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2.
\]
Both scores have norm at most \(B/\varepsilon\); hence
\[
 \|\widehat\xi_t\widehat\xi_t^\top-\xi_t\xi_t^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{2BD_1}{\varepsilon^2}\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2.
\]
After averaging and combining this inequality with the realized-minus-predictable-QV bound and the predictable-QV bound from Theorem 1, we obtain
\[
 \widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_J=O_P(T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T)=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. Likewise, smoothness gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|\widehat H_T-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le\|\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\frac{D_2}{\varepsilon}\|\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*\|_2\\
 &=O_P(T^{-1/2})=O_P(e_T).
\end{aligned}
\]
Restoring the fallback changes none of these uniform order statements because its probability tends uniformly to zero.

The last display and \(\sigma_{\min}(H)\ge h_-\) imply \(\sigma_{\min}(\widehat H_T)\ge h_-/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one. Basin nondegeneracy and \(\widehat\Omega_T-\Omega_J=o_P(1)\) similarly imply \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Omega_T)\ge\omega_-/2\) with probability tending uniformly to one. Therefore
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\longrightarrow0.
\]
On \(\mathcal E_T\),
\[
 \widehat H_T^{-1}-H^{-1}=\widehat H_T^{-1}(H-\widehat H_T)H^{-1},
\]
and \(\|\widehat H_T^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/h_-\). Expanding the two inverse factors and middle covariance factor in the sandwich gives
\[
 \widehat V_T-V_J=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The identity-matrix branch makes the statistic total at finite \(T\) and is entered with uniformly vanishing probability.

It remains to derive the pivot. Fix \(\|c\|_2=1\), put \(a=H^{-\top}c\), and set \(U_t=a^\top\xi_t\). Theorem 1 gives
\[
 (KD_1)^{-1}\le\|a\|_2\le h_-^{-1},
 \qquad |U_t|\le B/(\varepsilon h_-).
\]
Moreover, with probability tending uniformly to one,
\[
 A_T^2:=\sum_{t=1}^TE_P[U_t^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]
 =a^\top\langle S\rangle_Ta
 \ge\frac{\omega_-}{2(KD_1)^2}T.
\]
The first part of this proof also gives
\[
 a^\top([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)a=O_P(\sqrt T),
\]
so \(a^\top[S]_Ta/A_T^2\to_P1\) uniformly and \(P\{a^\top[S]_Ta>0\}\to1\) uniformly. The fourth-moment condition in the cited self-normalized martingale theorem holds with \(\delta=2\), because
\[
 \sum_{t=1}^TE_P|U_t|^4\le T\left(\frac{B}{\varepsilon h_-}\right)^4,
 \qquad A_T^4\ge C_-T^2
\]
outside an event of uniformly vanishing probability. Thus \(\mathrm{lem:saco\text{-}self\text{-}normalized\text{-}martingale\text{-}clt}\) yields
\[
 \frac{a^\top S_T}{\sqrt{a^\top[S]_Ta}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\]
This convergence is uniform in \(P\) and unit \(c\): otherwise a violating sequence \((P_T,c_T)\) would itself be a triangular array satisfying the same common increment, variance-growth, QV-ratio, and fourth-moment bounds, contradicting the cited theorem.

The exact-root linearization and the feasible covariance expansions give
\[
 \sqrt T\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)
 =-T^{-1/2}a^\top S_T+O_P(e_T)
\]
and
\[
 c^\top\widehat V_Tc=T^{-1}a^\top[S]_Ta+O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The denominator is bounded away from zero with probability tending uniformly to one, so division is legitimate there and
\[
 T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)
 =-\frac{a^\top S_T}{\sqrt{a^\top[S]_Ta}}+o_P(1)
\]
uniformly. Continuity of \(\Phi\) and the standard smoothing inequality for distribution functions now imply the asserted uniform Kolmogorov convergence. Finally,
\[
 P\{|N(0,1)|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\}=1-\alpha,
\]
which proves the Wald-coverage statement. The cited pointwise Saco pivot supplies the comparison claim; the uniform variance-growth, QV-ratio, feasible-inverse, and truncation controls used here were all derived from the frozen class primitives.

statements.statement:
Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence or subsequence for which the \(P_\ell\)-specific mixture parameters in Theorem 1 have a fixed support \(\mathcal J_0\), \(p_{P_\ell,j}\to p_j^\infty\), and \(V_{P_\ell,j}\to V_j^\infty\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\). Put \(\mathcal J_\infty=\{j\in\mathcal J_0:p_j^\infty>0\}\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if \(c^\top V_j^\infty c=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\). The necessity identifies the law of the limiting finite centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it is not a one-level variance-matching claim.
statements.justification: This theorem exactly characterizes every-level fixed-sandwich validity for one causal contrast along any convergent P-specific mixture subsequence.
statements.gap: Directional-stability work gives sufficient target-specific conditions and Saco highlights random predictable variance; neither gives the finite-mixture every-level converse with vanishing-weight atoms handled explicitly.
statements.consumer: Trial analysts can decide whether a deterministic variance report remains valid for one prespecified HeartSteps excursion-effect contrast even when other directions vary across regimes.
statements.proof_tex:
Set
\[
 q_j=c^\top V_j^\infty c>0,
 \qquad s=c^\top\Sigma c>0.
\]
Positive definiteness and \(c\ne0\) justify all divisions. The deterministic interval definition gives
\[
 \{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}
 =\left\{\left|\sqrt{T_\ell}\,c^\top(\widehat\theta_{T_\ell}-\theta^*)\right|
 \le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt s\right\}.
\]
Theorem 1's uniform finite-mixture approximation applies to the triangular sequence \(P_\ell\). The assumed convergence of its weights and covariance matrices, together with continuity of every centered normal CDF, therefore gives, for \(z=z_{1-\alpha/2}>0\),
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}
 =\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_\infty}p_j^\infty
 \left\{2\Phi\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{q_j}}\right)-1\right\}.
\]
If \(q_j=s\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\), the right side is \(2\Phi(z)-1=1-\alpha\), proving sufficiency.

Conversely, suppose the coverage limit equals \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). As \(\alpha\) ranges over \((0,1)\), \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) ranges over \((0,\infty)\). Hence
\[
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal J_\infty}p_j^\infty
 \left\{2\Phi\left(z\sqrt{\frac{s}{q_j}}\right)-1\right\}
 =2\Phi(z)-1
 \qquad(z>0).
\]
Let \(X\) have law \(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_\infty}p_j^\infty N(0,q_j)\). Both \(X/\sqrt s\) and a standard Gaussian are symmetric, so equality of their absolute-value distribution functions for every positive argument implies equality of their full laws. The mixture is finite, hence its second and fourth moments exist. Equality of laws gives
\[
 \sum_jp_j^\infty q_j=s,
 \qquad 3\sum_jp_j^\infty q_j^2=3s^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \sum_jp_j^\infty(q_j-s)^2
 =\sum_jp_j^\infty q_j^2-2s\sum_jp_j^\infty q_j+s^2\sum_jp_j^\infty=0.
\]
Every weight indexed by \(\mathcal J_\infty\) is strictly positive and every summand is nonnegative, so \(q_j=s\) for every such \(j\). This proves necessity. Requiring every nominal level is essential because it supplies equality for all \(z>0\); the proof makes no inference from one accidental coverage equality.

statements.statement: Along any sequence or subsequence with limiting mixture parameters \((p_j^\infty,V_j^\infty)_{j\in\mathcal J_\infty}\) as in Theorem 3, a single deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if \(V_j^\infty=\Sigma\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\). Equivalently, the limiting selected covariance that equals \(V_j^\infty\) with probability \(p_j^\infty\) is almost surely the deterministic matrix \(\Sigma\). In the fixed-parameter special case this is equivalent to \(V_J=\Sigma\) almost surely. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality follows by polarization.
statements.justification: This theorem separates target-specific validity from target-agnostic covariance invariance on the same positive-weight limiting mixture support.
statements.gap: Shen and coauthors distinguish directional from matrix stability on the sufficiency side; the finite-mixture every-level necessity and polarization argument remain unstated.
statements.consumer: Software reporting many adaptive-experiment contrasts can use the theorem to determine whether one fixed covariance matrix is defensible.
statements.proof_tex:
Suppose first that one deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\) gives the asserted subsequential coverage for every nonzero \(c\) and every nominal level. The contrastwise theorem gives
\[
 c^\top(V_j^\infty-\Sigma)c=0
 \qquad\text{for every }c\ne0\text{ and every }j\in\mathcal J_\infty.
\]
Fix \(j\) and set \(A=V_j^\infty-\Sigma\), which is symmetric. Taking \(c=e_r\) gives \(A_{rr}=0\). For \(r\ne s\), taking \(c=e_r+e_s\) and using the diagonal equalities gives
\[
 0=(e_r+e_s)^\top A(e_r+e_s)=2A_{rs}.
\]
Thus every entry of \(A\) vanishes and \(V_j^\infty=\Sigma\).

Conversely, if \(V_j^\infty=\Sigma\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\), then \(c^\top V_j^\infty c=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every nonzero \(c\). The contrastwise theorem gives coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every such \(c\) and every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).

Let \(V_\infty\) denote the random matrix taking value \(V_j^\infty\) with probability \(p_j^\infty\). If all \(V_j^\infty\) equal \(\Sigma\), then \(V_\infty=\Sigma\) almost surely. Conversely, if \(V_\infty=A\) almost surely for a deterministic matrix \(A\), then each event selecting \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\) has positive probability and forces \(V_j^\infty=A\). In the fixed-parameter case, the definition \(V_J=\sum_j\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\) gives the same argument with \(V_\infty\) replaced by \(V_J\).

statements.statement: For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/6)\), the bounded witness \(P^{\dagger}\) belongs at every \(T\ge2\) to a class \(\mathfrak P_T\) with common choices \(B=2\), \(D_1=D_2=1\), \(h_-=1\), \(L_\Pi=1/12\), \(\omega_-=1\), \(\kappa(u)=u\), \(s_\Theta=1\), \(\rho=\varepsilon/8\), \(r_T=1/(2T)\), and \(\delta_T=0\). Specifically, the policy floor is \(1/6\), \(\sup_{a,\theta}\|g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta)\|_2<2\), the derivative and curvature bounds are \(1\) and \(0\), \(M_{P^{\dagger}}(\theta)=-\theta\), every empirical moment admits an exact minimum of zero in \(\Theta\), and \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J\|_2=1/(2T)\) almost surely. Moreover, \(P^{\dagger}(J=1)=2/5\), \(P^{\dagger}(J=2)=3/5\), so \(\mathcal J=\{1,2\}\); tail selection is exact after the first assignment, \(H=-I_2\), \(\Omega_1=V_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\), and \(\Omega_2=V_2=\operatorname{diag}(1,3)\). Hence for \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\), \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c=1\) in both positive-mass basins although \(V_1\ne V_2\), so contrastwise deterministic-sandwich validity holds while matrixwise invariance fails.
statements.justification: This elementary bounded construction verifies inside the stated law class that the contrastwise and matrixwise frontiers are logically distinct.
statements.gap: This is a non-novel existence witness, not evidence about the Guo--Xu recursion; its role is to prevent the directional and matrix claims from being conflated by an unattained free-matrix example.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts can retain a valid primary-endpoint interval in a concrete adaptive experiment without claiming that all secondary contrasts share a stable covariance.
statements.proof_tex:
We verify every primitive defining the class. The full-data vectors are i.i.d. because the two Rademacher potential outcomes are independent across occasions and arms and the context is constant. At each occasion the displayed policy is a function of the past-measurable state, and the action is drawn from that logged policy independently of the current potential outcomes, so sequential randomization holds.

At \(\eta=0\) and \(\eta=1\), the arm-probability vectors are
\[
 (2/5,1/4,7/20),\qquad(2/5,1/6,13/30).
\]
Linear interpolation preserves their coordinatewise minima, so every arm probability is at least \(1/6>\varepsilon\). The three coordinate slopes are \(0,-1/12,1/12\), respectively, proving the policy-Lipschitz condition with \(L_\Pi=1/12\).

For \(\theta\in[-1,1]^2\),
\[
 \sup|Y_t(1)-\theta_1|\le1+\sqrt{2/5}<2,
 \qquad
 \sup|Y_t(2)-\theta_2|\le1+\sqrt{1/2}<2.
\]
Each score has only one possibly nonzero coordinate, so \(B=2\) is valid. The derivative matrices are \(\operatorname{diag}(-1,0)\), \(\operatorname{diag}(0,-1)\), and zero. Their operator norms are at most one and all second derivatives vanish, so \(D_1=D_2=1\) are valid envelopes. Direct expectation gives
\[
 M_{P^\dagger}(\theta)=(-\theta_1,-\theta_2)^\top=-\theta,
 \qquad H=-I_2.
\]
Thus \(\theta^*=0\) is the unique root, \(\|M_{P^\dagger}(\theta)\|_2=\|\theta\|_2\), \(\kappa(u)=u\) is valid, \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial[-1,1]^2)=1\), and \(\sigma_{\min}(H)=1\).

Every realized empirical moment has a zero in \(\Theta\). If arm \(a\in\{1,2\}\) is observed, choose \(\theta_a\) as the average of its observed outcomes with positive weights \(1/\pi_t(a)\); it lies in the convex hull of that arm's two outcome values. If the arm is never observed, its empirical coordinate moment is identically zero and any coordinate in \([-1,1]\) works. The two coordinates separate, so these choices make \(G_T(\theta)=0\), proving that its norm has exact minimum zero.

At the first occasion the state is \(1/2\), and the arm-one probability remains \(2/5\). Hence
\[
 P^\dagger(J=1)=P^\dagger(A_1=1)=2/5,
 \qquad P^\dagger(J=2)=3/5.
\]
For every \(t\ge1\), \(\eta_t=\bar\eta_J\), while \(|\eta_0-\bar\eta_J|=1/2\). Therefore
\[
 T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T|\eta_{t-1}-\bar\eta_J|=\frac1{2T}
\]
almost surely. Tail selection holds, the attraction condition holds with \(r_T=1/(2T)\) and \(\delta_T=0\), and \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+1/(2T)\to0\). Also
\[
 0<\rho=\varepsilon/8<\min\{1,\varepsilon/(4D_2)\},
\]
as required.

At \(\theta^*=0\), only arms one and two contribute to the covariance. Since \(E[Y_t(1)^2]=2/5\) and \(E[Y_t(2)^2]=1/2\),
\[
 \Omega_1=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{2/5}{2/5},\frac{1/2}{1/4}\right)
 =\operatorname{diag}(1,2),
\]
and
\[
 \Omega_2=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{2/5}{2/5},\frac{1/2}{1/6}\right)
 =\operatorname{diag}(1,3).
\]
Both dominate \(I_2\), so \(\omega_-=1\) is valid. Because \(H=-I_2\), the sandwich definition gives \(V_j=\Omega_j\). This verifies every class condition with constants independent of \(T\).

Finally, for \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) and \(c=(1,0)^\top\),
\[
 c^\top V_1c=c^\top V_2c=c^\top\Sigma c=1,
 \qquad V_1\ne V_2.
\]
The constant sequence has fixed weights \((2/5,3/5)\) and fixed covariance matrices, so it is a valid instance of the corrected subsequential theorems. Their contrastwise and matrixwise conclusions give exactly the claimed separation without invoking label-stable convergence.

statements.statement:
Consider the bounded-noise Guo--Xu recursion with arbitrary fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0\) and deterministic tie arm \(1\). Put \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and, for \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\), define
\[
 h(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+16v}{2},\frac{17-u-16v}{2},
                 \frac{u-4v}{4},\frac{-3-u+4v}{24}\right).
\]
For \(t\ge1\), put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), and \(\Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t)\). Then \(q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=O(t^{-1})\) almost surely, \(\Psi_t\) obeys an exact stochastic-approximation recursion with step \(1/(t+1)\), and its affine interpolation is a bounded perturbed solution, hence an asymptotic pseudotrajectory, of the closed convexified inclusion \(\dot\psi\in F(\psi)\) below. Writing \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\), \(h_+=h(p,q)\), \(h_-=h(q,p)\), \(h_1=h(p,p)\), and \(h_2=h(q,q)\), its graph on \(d_1,d_2>0\) is
\[
 F(\psi)=
 \begin{cases}
  \{h_+-\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)>0,\\
  \{h_--\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)<0,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1<d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1>d_2,\\
  \operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1=d_2.
 \end{cases}
\]
Every almost-sure normalized-state limit set is internally chain transitive for \(F\) and is contained in the computable parallelogram \(\mathcal C=\{h(u,v):(u,v)\in[q,p]^2\}\); the projected slope limit set is its continuous image under \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\).

The smaller inclusion having only \(h_+-\psi\), \(h_--\psi\), and \(\operatorname{co}\{h_+-\psi,h_--\psi\}\) on the switching surface is not a valid unconditional reduction of this recursion. If it were the limiting inclusion, its only internally chain-transitive sets would be the three singletons \(\{h_-\}\), \(\{h(u_0,1-u_0)\}\), and \(\{h_+\}\), where
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},\qquad
 \frac{N_1}{D_1}=\frac{N_2}{D_2}
 =b_0:=\frac{\sqrt{4609}-91}{1224}
 \quad\text{at }h(u_0,1-u_0).
\]
The correct graph instead has an uncountable family of additional internally chain-transitive singleton equilibria. Explicitly, for
\[
 u\in[u_0,p],\qquad
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32},
\]
one has \(h(u,v(u))\in\mathcal C\), equal slope coordinates, first normalized Gram coordinate smaller than the second, and \(0\in F(h(u,v(u)))\). In particular,
\[
 v_*:=v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}
\]
gives an equilibrium \(h(p,v_*)\) distinct from \(h_-\), \(h(u_0,1-u_0)\), and \(h_+\). This continuum is an explicit internally-chain-transitive obstruction to a three-candidate conclusion from the standard differential-inclusion route.

For the actual recursion, on \(\mathcal L_+=\{\liminf_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})>0\}\) and \(\mathcal L_-=\{\limsup_t(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})<0\}\), respectively,
\[
 (\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
 \longrightarrow
 \left(\frac{19}{46},-\frac{79}{3804}\right)^\top
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \left(-\frac{79}{634},\frac{19}{276}\right)^\top.
\]
Both events have probability bounded away from zero uniformly over \(\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}\), and the corresponding pathwise Cesaro errors converge to zero. If both slopes have a common-coordinate subsequential limit and \((u,v)\) is a simultaneous subsequential limit of the empirical conditional arm-\(1\) rates, then necessarily
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
The relation \(v=1-u\), and hence the candidate \((u_0,b_0)\), is justified only if same-arm switching-layer occupation is separately excluded; the exact recursion does not provide that exclusion. Consequently, this argument proves neither finite almost-sure tail selection nor zero probability of switching-surface convergence. It also proves no compact-initial-set uniform attraction moduli \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\). These are dynamics-only conclusions: they assert neither membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) nor applicability of any inference theorem.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\mu _1=1/2\), \(\mu _2=1/12\), \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), and \(C_{t,a}=\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}\).  The recursion in \(\textnormal{def:guoxu-recursion}\) gives, for every \(t\geq 1\),
\[
 D_{t,a}=1+\sum_{s=1}^t C_{s,a}X_s^2,\qquad
 N_{t,a}=\eta_{0,a}+\sum_{s=1}^t C_{s,a}X_s(\mu_a+\sigma_aR_{s,a}),\qquad
 \widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=\frac{N_{t,a}}{D_{t,a}}. \tag{1}
\]
The clipped randomization assigns either arm with conditional probability at least \(q\).  Because \(X_s\) is independent of \(\mathcal F_{s-1}\) and uniform on \(\{-4,1\}\),
\[
 E[C_{s,a}X_s^2\mid\mathcal F_{s-1}]
 \geq qE[X_s^2]=\frac{17}{200}. \tag{2}
\]
We first record the elementary bounded-martingale argument used repeatedly below.  If \((U_s)\) is a scalar martingale-difference sequence with \(|U_s|\leq L\), orthogonality gives \(E(\sum_{s\leq n}U_s)^2\leq L^2n\).  At \(n=k^2\), Chebyshev's inequality gives a summable upper bound \(L^2/(\epsilon^2k^2)\) for \(k^{-2}|\sum_{s\leq k^2}U_s|>\epsilon\).  The first Borel--Cantelli conclusion follows directly here from the union bound
\[
 P\!\left(\bigcup_{k\geq K}\left\{\left|\sum_{s\leq k^2}U_s\right|>\epsilon k^2\right\}\right)
 \leq \frac{L^2}{\epsilon^2}\sum_{k\geq K}k^{-2}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus \(k^{-2}\sum_{s\leq k^2}U_s\to0\) almost surely.  The at most \(2k+1\) bounded increments between \(k^2\) and \((k+1)^2\) fill the gaps, proving \(n^{-1}\sum_{s\leq n}U_s\to0\) almost surely.

Apply this result to \(C_{s,a}X_s^2-E[C_{s,a}X_s^2\mid\mathcal F_{s-1}]\).  Equations (1)--(2) yield
\[
 \liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{D_{t,a}}t\geq\frac{17}{200},
 \qquad q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}=D_{t,a}^{-1}=O(t^{-1})quad\hbox{almost surely}. \tag{3}
\]
The same argument applies to \(C_{s,a}X_sR_{s,a}\): by the ordering in \(\textnormal{def:guoxu-recursion}\), the action is randomized before the reward innovation is observed, and that innovation is conditionally centered.  Hence
\[
 t^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^tC_{s,a}X_sR_{s,a}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\hbox{almost surely}. \tag{4}
\]
Moreover, (1) expresses each slope as a convex combination of its initial value \(\eta_{0,a}\) and the observed ratios \(Y_s(a)/X_s\), with weights \(1\) and \(C_{s,a}X_s^2\).  The envelope \(M_{\mathrm{GX}}\) therefore bounds both slopes.  Together with bounded \(X_s\) and bounded Rademacher rewards, this bounds every coordinate of \(\Psi_t\); by (3), both normalized Gram coordinates are eventually bounded away from zero.

Define
\[
 U_{t+1}=\bigl(C_{t+1,1}X_{t+1}^2,C_{t+1,2}X_{t+1}^2,
 C_{t+1,1}X_{t+1}Y_{t+1}(1),C_{t+1,2}X_{t+1}Y_{t+1}(2)\bigr).
\]
Dividing the four sufficient-statistic updates by \(t+1\) gives the exact stochastic-approximation recursion
\[
 \Psi_{t+1}-\Psi_t=\frac1{t+1}(U_{t+1}-\Psi_t). \tag{5}
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal F_t\), let \(u_t\) and \(v_t\) be the arm-one assignment probabilities at contexts \(1\) and \(-4\), respectively.  Conditional centering of the rewards and direct averaging over the two equally likely contexts give
\[
 E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]=h(u_t,v_t), \tag{6}
\]
because the four coordinates on the right are
\[
 \frac{u_t+16v_t}{2},\qquad \frac{17-u_t-16v_t}{2},\qquad
 \mu_1\frac{u_t-4v_t}{2},\qquad
 \mu_2\frac{-3-u_t+4v_t}{2}.
\]
This is precisely the displayed formula for \(h\).

For \(\psi=(d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\), put \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\).  At the current normalized state,
\[
 b_t:=\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}}-\sqrt{q^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}}
 =t^{-1/2}\bigl(d_{t,1}^{-1/2}-d_{t,2}^{-1/2}\bigr). \tag{7}
\]
The arm-one minus arm-two UCB index has the sign of \(\Delta(\Psi_t)+b_t\) at context \(1\), and the sign of \(b_t-\Delta(\Psi_t)\) at context \(-4\).  Equation (3) gives \(|b_t|=O(t^{-1/2})\).  Consequently, away from \(\Delta=0\), the two greedy choices are eventually opposite: \((u_t,v_t)=(p,q)\) for \(\Delta>0\), and \((u_t,v_t)=(q,p)\) for \(\Delta<0\).  On \(\Delta=0\), equation (7) has the sign of \(d_2-d_1\).  Thus both contexts make arm one greedy when \(d_1<d_2\), both make arm two greedy when \(d_1>d_2\), and the specified deterministic tie rule makes arm one greedy when \(d_1=d_2\).  The corresponding conditional means are \(h_1,h_2,h_1\), respectively.

This calculation gives the asserted closed convexified graph.  To verify the perturbation condition explicitly, observe that a same-arm mode can occur off the switching surface only if \(|\Delta(\Psi_t)|\leq |b_t|\).  On the eventual compact region already obtained, replace \(n_1\) by \(n_1-d_1\Delta(\Psi_t)\), leaving the other coordinates fixed.  The resulting point lies on \(\Delta=0\) and is within a fixed multiple of \(|\Delta(\Psi_t)|\) of \(\Psi_t\).  Therefore, for a deterministic \(c_0<\infty\),
\[
 E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]-\Psi_t\in F^{\delta_t}(\Psi_t),
 \qquad \delta_t=c_0t^{-1/2}\longrightarrow0, \tag{8}
\]
where \(F^\delta\) denotes the graph enlargement.  The atoms \(h_+\) and \(h_-\) at every switching point make the graph closed under approach from the two open half-spaces; the atom \(h_1\), respectively \(h_2\), records approach within the switching layer when \(d_1<d_2\), respectively \(d_1>d_2\); and all four atoms at \(d_1=d_2\) close the remaining approaches.  Hence the displayed graph has nonempty compact convex values and is closed.  Its velocities have linear growth because its four atoms are fixed.  Outside a compact convex region containing the eventual trajectory, compose the atom correspondence with metric projection and retain the term \(-\psi\); this supplies a global extension with the same properties without changing the eventual dynamics.

Let \(M_{t+1}=U_{t+1}-E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]\) and \(\gamma_t=1/t\).  Each coordinate is a bounded martingale difference.  Stopping its weighted partial sum at the first crossing of \(\epsilon\) and using orthogonality of the stopped increments gives, for every coordinate and every \(j\),
\[
 P\!\left\{\sup_{k\geq2^j}\left|\sum_{s=2^j}^k\gamma_{s+1}M_{s+1}\right|>\epsilon\right\}
 \leq \frac{C}{\epsilon^2}\sum_{s=2^j}^{\infty}\gamma_{s+1}^2
 \leq\frac{C'}{\epsilon^22^j}. \tag{9}
\]
The right side is summable in \(j\), so the same union-bound argument used above shows that the weighted martingale tails vanish almost surely, uniformly over every bounded interval of stochastic-approximation time.  Equations (5), (8), and (9), together with boundedness of \(\Psi_t\), verify the bounded-perturbed-solution hypotheses of \(\textnormal{lem:bhs-perturbed-limit-set}\).  That lemma makes the affine interpolation an asymptotic pseudotrajectory and makes its limit set internally chain transitive.

Let
\[
 \mathcal C=h([q,p]^2)=\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}.
\]
Every velocity in \(F(\psi)\) is \(z-\psi\) for some \(z\in\mathcal C\).  If \(P_{\mathcal C}\psi\) is the Euclidean projection and \(V(\psi)=\operatorname{dist}(\psi,\mathcal C)^2\), the projection inequality gives, along every solution and for almost every time outside \(\mathcal C\),
\[
 \frac{d}{ds}V(\psi(s))
 =2(\psi-P_{\mathcal C}\psi)^\top(z-\psi)
 \leq-2\|\psi-P_{\mathcal C}\psi\|_2^2=-2V(\psi). \tag{10}
\]
If a solution starts in \(\mathcal C\), variation of constants writes it as a convex combination of its initial point and a weighted average of points \(z(s)\in\mathcal C\); hence \(\mathcal C\) is positively invariant.  Thus \(V\) is a continuous Lyapunov function for \(\mathcal C\), and \(V(\mathcal C)=\{0\}\) has empty interior.  By \(\textnormal{lem:bhs-lyapunov-ict}\), every internally chain-transitive normalized-state limit set lies in \(\mathcal C\).  Equation (3) keeps \(d_1,d_2\) positive on that limit set, so the slope projection \((d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\mapsto(n_1/d_1,n_2/d_2)\) is continuous there.  This proves the first paragraph of the claim.

We next identify exactly what the tempting two-mode inclusion would imply.  Let \(\mathcal C_0=\operatorname{co}\{h_-,h_+\}\) and write its points uniquely as \(h_-+\lambda(h_+-h_-)\), \(0\leq\lambda\leq1\).  Equivalently,
\[
 u=q+(p-q)\lambda,\qquad v=p-(p-q)\lambda=1-u. \tag{11}
\]
Cross-multiplication is legitimate because both Gram coordinates are positive, and direct expansion gives
\[
 \Delta(h(u,v))=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 f(u,v):=u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0; \tag{12}
\]
indeed, after multiplication by the positive common denominator, the numerator of the slope difference is \(-5f(u,v)\).  Substitution of \(v=1-u\) yields \(f(u,1-u)=-75u^2+47u+8\).  Its unique root in \([q,p]\) is
\[
 u_0=\frac{47+\sqrt{4609}}{150},
\]
and substitution into either slope ratio gives \(b_0=(\sqrt{4609}-91)/1224\).

On \(\mathcal C_0\), the two-mode inclusion reduces to
\[
 \dot\lambda=-\lambda\quad(\lambda<\lambda_0),\qquad
 \dot\lambda=1-\lambda\quad(\lambda>\lambda_0),\qquad
 \dot\lambda\in[-\lambda_0,1-\lambda_0]\quad(\lambda=\lambda_0), \tag{13}
\]
where \(u_0=q+(p-q)\lambda_0\).  Distance squared to \(\mathcal C_0\) first confines every internally chain-transitive set to the segment by the argument of (10).  On the segment, the continuous function
\[
 W(\lambda)=
 \begin{cases}
 \lambda/\lambda_0,&0\leq\lambda\leq\lambda_0,\\
 (1-\lambda)/(1-\lambda_0),&\lambda_0\leq\lambda\leq1
 \end{cases}
\]
strictly decreases along every nonconstant solution outside \(\{0,\lambda_0,1\}\) and never increases from those three points.  Since \(W(\{0,\lambda_0,1\})=\{0,1\}\) has empty interior, \(\textnormal{lem:bhs-lyapunov-ict}\) puts every internally chain-transitive set inside \(\{0,\lambda_0,1\}\) with \(W\) constant.  The set \(\{0,1\}\) is not internally chain transitive: for \(\epsilon<1/3\), the solutions from its endpoints are constant, so no \((\epsilon,S)\)-chain contained in that two-point set can travel from one endpoint to the other.  Thus only the three asserted singletons are internally chain transitive for the smaller inclusion.

That smaller graph cannot approximate the recursion uniformly near the switching surface.  If \(\Delta=0\) and \(d_1<d_2\), equation (7) makes arm one greedy at both contexts and the conditional mean is \(h_1\).  But \(h_1\notin\mathcal C_0\): the affine map \((u,v)\mapsto h(u,v)\) is injective, every parameter pair on \(\mathcal C_0\) satisfies \(u+v=1\), and \(h_1\) corresponds to \((p,p)\), whose sum is \(2p\neq1\).  Compactness therefore gives \(\operatorname{dist}(h_1,\mathcal C_0)>0\).  The \(O(t^{-1/2})\) bonus cannot be discarded uniformly in the \(O(t^{-1/2})\) switching layer.

The extra internally chain-transitive sets of the correct graph are computable.  Solving (12) for its smaller \(v\)-root gives
\[
 v(u)=\frac{3u+18-\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}{32}. \tag{14}
\]
For \(u\in[u_0,p]\), substitution verifies \(f(u,v(u))=0\) and \(v(u_0)=1-u_0\).  Direct differentiation gives
\[
 v'(u)=\frac1{32}\left(3+\frac{228-50u}{2\sqrt{25u^2-228u+324}}\right)>0, \tag{15}
\]
because \(u\leq p<1\).  The elementary bounds \(67<\sqrt{4609}<68\) and \(73<\sqrt{5457}<74\) imply
\[
 0.23<v(u_0)<0.24,\qquad 0.308<v(p)<0.314.
\]
Consequently \(q<u,v(u)<p\), \(u+v(u)\geq1\), and
\[
 u+16v(u)\leq p+16v(p)<p+16(0.314)<6.014<\frac{17}{2}. \tag{16}
\]
The first two inequalities put \((u,v(u))\) in the triangle with vertices \((p,q),(q,p),(p,p)\), while (16) says that the first Gram coordinate of \(h(u,v(u))\) is smaller than the second.  Therefore
\[
 h(u,v(u))\in\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\},\qquad
 \Delta(h(u,v(u)))=0,\qquad 0\in F(h(u,v(u))). \tag{17}
\]
Each singleton in (17) is an equilibrium and hence internally chain transitive.  The map \(h\) is injective because the two linear forms \(u+16v\) and \(u-4v\) have nonzero determinant; the family is therefore uncountable.  At \(u=p\), equation (14) simplifies to
\[
 v(p)=\frac{2097}{3200}-\frac{3\sqrt{5457}}{640}=v_*,
\]
and the bounds above show that this equilibrium differs from the three two-mode candidates.  This proves the stated obstruction.

It remains to separate what the exact recursion itself establishes from what the enlarged inclusion merely permits.  Put \(\Delta_t=\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1}-\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}\).  On \(\mathcal L_+\), equation (3) makes the bonus vanish while \(\Delta_t\) is eventually bounded below by a positive constant.  Hence eventually arm one is greedy at context \(1\) and arm two at context \(-4\).  Applying the bounded martingale law proved above to the four context--action counts, and using (4) for the reward noise, gives
\[
 \frac1t(D_{t,1},D_{t,2},N_{t,1},N_{t,2})
 \longrightarrow h_+=\left(\frac{23}{40},\frac{317}{40},\frac{19}{80},-\frac{79}{480}\right). \tag{18}
\]
Equations (1) and (18) yield the first displayed slope limit.  The identical argument on \(\mathcal L_-\) gives
\[
 \frac1t(D_{t,1},D_{t,2},N_{t,1},N_{t,2})
 \longrightarrow h_-=\left(\frac{317}{40},\frac{23}{40},-\frac{79}{80},\frac{19}{480}\right), \tag{19}
\]
and hence the second displayed slope limit.  The limiting slope gaps are, respectively,
\[
 \frac{19}{46}+\frac{79}{3804}=\frac{37955}{87492}>0,
 \qquad
 -\frac{79}{634}-\frac{19}{276}=-\frac{16925}{87492}<0. \tag{20}
\]

We now prove the uniform positive-probability assertion rather than infer it from the differential inclusion.  Fix a sufficiently large even \(n\).  For the positive regime, prescribe a length-\(2n\) history consisting first of \(n\) observations with \(X=1,A=1\), then \(n\) observations with \(X=-4,A=2\), and prescribe equally many positive and negative Rademacher signs for each selected arm.  Each prescribed context has probability \(1/2\), each prescribed action has conditional probability at least \(q\), and each prescribed relevant sign has probability \(1/2\).  Thus this history has probability at least \((q/4)^{2n}\), uniformly over \(\eta_0\in[-1,1]^2\).  At its end the slopes are exactly
\[
 \frac{\eta_{0,1}+n/2}{1+n},\qquad
 \frac{\eta_{0,2}-n/3}{1+16n}, \tag{21}
\]
which converge uniformly in \(\eta_0\) to \(1/2\) and \(-1/48\), and both inverse Gram coordinates are \(O(n^{-1})\).

Consider after this prefix the reference policy that makes arm one greedy at context \(1\) and arm two greedy at context \(-4\).  After \(k\) further steps, its conditional-mean sufficient statistics are obtained by adding \(kh_+\) to the four terminal statistics in (21).  Each resulting armwise slope is a ratio \((a+kb)/(c+kd)\) with positive \(c,d\), and hence is a denominator-weighted average of \(a/c\) and \(b/d\).  By (20)--(21), there are constants \(\gamma_0>0\) and \(n_0<\infty\), independent of \(\eta_0\), such that for \(n\geq n_0\) these two reference slopes differ by at least \(3\gamma_0\) for every \(k\geq0\).  Their Gram coordinates are at least a fixed positive multiple of \(n+k\), so the absolute difference of their UCB bonuses is at most \(C(n+k)^{-1/2}\).  Increasing \(n_0\) makes this bound at most \(\gamma_0\).

For completeness, couple the actual rule and this reference rule with the same contexts, rewards, and randomization uniforms, and let \(\zeta\) be the first future occasion at which their greedy arms differ.  Up to \(\zeta\), subtracting the conditional mean \(h_+\) from each sufficient-statistic increment gives four stopped martingales with a common bounded-increment constant depending only on the fixed \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2\).  The stopping-time orthogonality argument used for (9), followed by a union bound over dyadic blocks, yields for every fixed \(\gamma>0\)
\[
 P\!\left(\sup_{k\geq0}\frac{\|M_{k\wedge\zeta}\|_\infty}{n+k}>\gamma
 \mathrel{\Big|}\hbox{the prescribed prefix}\right)
 \leq \frac{C_\gamma}{n}. \tag{22}
\]
Indeed, on the block \(2^jn\leq n+k<2^{j+1}n\), a crossing requires a stopped partial sum of size at least \(\gamma2^jn\), whereas its second moment is at most a constant times \(2^{j+1}n\); summing the resulting bounds \(C/(\gamma^22^jn)\) over \(j\geq0\) and over four coordinates proves (22).

Because all reference denominators are bounded below by a constant times \(n+k\), the ratio map is uniformly Lipschitz under the relative perturbation in (22).  Choose \(\gamma\) small enough both to preserve a positive constant lower bound for the perturbed denominators and to change the slope gap by at most \(\gamma_0\).  The same denominator bound makes the actual bonus difference \(O((n+k)^{-1/2})\); enlarge \(n_0\) once more so that it is at most \(\gamma_0\).  On the complementary event in (22), the actual slope gap is therefore at least \(2\gamma_0\), while its bonus difference is at most \(\gamma_0\).  The two UCB inequalities retain the reference greedy arms at the putative first exit, a contradiction.  Thus \(\zeta=\infty\) on that event.  Taking \(n\) still larger so that \(C_\gamma/n\leq1/2\) proves
\[
 \inf_{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}P_{\eta_0}(\mathcal L_+)
 \geq \frac12(q/4)^{2n}>0. \tag{23}
\]
For the negative regime, prescribe first \(n\) observations with \(X=-4,A=1\), then \(n\) with \(X=1,A=2\), again balancing the selected Rademacher signs.  The terminal slopes converge uniformly to \(-1/8\) and \(1/12\); the conditional-mean continuation adds \(kh_-\), and the second strict gap in (20) supplies the same stopped-martingale bootstrap.  Consequently
\[
 \inf_{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}P_{\eta_0}(\mathcal L_-)>0. \tag{24}
\]
On either event the corresponding slope sequence converges.  If \(\beta^+\) and \(\beta^-\) denote the two displayed deterministic limits, the elementary Cesaro lemma therefore gives, respectively,
\[
 \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\left\|\bigl(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}\bigr)^\top-\beta^+\right\|_2\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\left\|\bigl(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2}\bigr)^\top-\beta^-\right\|_2\longrightarrow0.
\]
This is the asserted pathwise Cesaro-error conclusion.

Finally, define the empirical conditional arm-one rates
\[
 u_T=\frac2T\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{X_t=1,A_t=1\},\qquad
 v_T=\frac2T\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{X_t=-4,A_t=1\}.
\]
The conditional arm-one probability at either context is always in \([q,p]\).  Applying the bounded martingale law to each centered context--action indicator, and to each centered context indicator, shows that every subsequential limit of \((u_T,v_T)\) lies in \([q,p]^2\).  If along a common subsequence both slopes tend to a common coordinate and \((u_T,v_T)\to(u,v)\), then (1), (4), and the context-count law give
\[
 \frac1T(D_{T,1},D_{T,2},N_{T,1},N_{T,2})\longrightarrow h(u,v).
\]
The denominators in this limit are positive because \((u,v)\in[q,p]^2\).  Equality of the two limiting slope ratios is therefore equivalent, by (12), to
\[
 u^2+12uv-21u-64v^2+72v=0.
\]
If same-arm switching-layer occupation is excluded, only the two opposite-context modes remain and (11) forces \(v=1-u\), producing \((u_0,b_0)\).  But (7) and the continuum in (14)--(17) show that this exclusion is not a consequence of the exact recursion or of the differential-inclusion theorem: same-arm modes survive throughout the shrinking switching layer.  The graph is discontinuous there, and the preceding argument supplies neither an avoidance estimate for switching-surface convergence nor a quantitative hitting, escape, or equicontinuity estimate uniform over compact initial sets.  It therefore establishes neither finite almost-sure tail selection nor zero switching-surface probability, and it does not establish compact-uniform moduli \(r_T(K_0),\delta_T(K_0)\).  Since membership in \(\mathfrak P_T\) requires precisely such tail-selection and uniform-attraction properties, no membership or inference conclusion is asserted.  This proves all parts of the theorem.
statements.justification: The normalized sufficient-statistic recursion gives the strongest rigorous dynamics certificate currently available: it proves the two separated limits and exposes an uncountable switching-equilibrium obstruction in the correct limiting differential inclusion.
statements.gap: The differential-inclusion limit set need not be one of three candidates because the vanishing UCB bonus produces same-arm modes inside the shrinking switching layer. Actual selection within that layer, zero probability of switching convergence, and compact-initial-set uniform attraction still require quantitative escape and equicontinuity estimates not supplied here.

Let \(p\in[1,\infty)\), \(\gamma>0\), and let \((X_i,\mathcal G_i)_{i=1}^n\) be a scalar martingale-difference sequence with \(n\ge2\) and \(\max_i\|X_i\|_\infty\le\gamma\). Put \(s^2=\sum_{i=1}^nE[X_i^2]\), \(V^2=s^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^nE[X_i^2\mid\mathcal G_{i-1}]\), and \(D=\sup_x|P\{s^{-1}\sum_iX_i\le x\}-\Phi(x)|\). There is a constant \(C_{p,\gamma}\) such that
\[
D\le C_{p,\gamma}\left\{\frac{n\log n}{s^3}+\left(\|V^2-1\|_p^p+s^{-2p}\right)^{1/(2p+1)}\right\}.
\]

Let \((X_{n,t},\mathcal G_{n,t})_{t=1}^{k_n}\) be a scalar martingale-difference array, \(S_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}\), \(Q_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}^2\), and \(A_n^2=\sum_tE[X_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}]\). If \(A_n^2\to\infty\) in probability, \(P(Q_n>0)\to1\), \(Q_n/A_n^2\to1\) in probability, and for some \(\delta>0\),
\[
 A_n^{-(2+\delta)}\sum_tE[|X_{n,t}|^{2+\delta}]\to0,
\]
then \(S_n/\sqrt{Q_n}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).
